analysis.title: RBC Luxury Datawatch: 3Q26 earnings season supports preference for BCU, ZGN, ADS, EL
key_insights: Luxury 3Q26 results were softer than expected on average. Growth is diverging between absolute luxury (Brunello Cucinelli, Zegna brand, Hermes Leather) and fashion-oriented luxury (LVMH, Kering, Hermes non-Leather, Moncler).

China was the main drag on luxury and RBC expects it to persist near term without macro improvement. Negative wealth effects in the US, cost-of-living pressure in Europe and weak inbound tourism are seen as incremental headwinds.

Positioning is skewed to defensive names (Brunello Cucinelli, Zegna) while Hermes' perception has weakened. Sentiment is soft on cyclical luxury names (LVMH, Kering) that need an inflexion. Investor interest is largely hedge fund oriented.

Luxury share prices were broadly flat over the last month. Zegna rose 10%, Brunello Cucinelli 7% and Burberry 6%, while Kering fell 21%. EPS revisions were modestly positive for Brunello Cucinelli and Zegna and negative for Kering, LVMH and Hermes.

Sporting goods 3Q26 was mixed. adidas beat consensus and raised FY26E guidance, Nike was soft with an FY27E outlook downgrade, and Puma's topline beat but elevated opex produced an EBIT miss. The group re-rated 26% on the month on average, helped by Nike EPS cuts.

adidas sentiment is improving as the market worries less about slowing growth into 2H26E and tough 1H27E comps. RBC cites FY27E visibility at 14x CY27E P/E and a 16%/24% EBIT/EPS 3-year CAGR. Nike has been quiet post 1Q27 results ahead of its November CMD.

EssilorLuxottica 3Q26 was reassuring, with Core growth of +6.5% organic and a +0.7% Wearables contribution. The debate is shifting to Core quality, and RBC sees modest FY26E and FY27E margin upside from mix and FX. Shares are up 27% over the last month on a roughly 5x multiple re-rating.
Stock picks into 4Q26E are Richemont, EssilorLuxottica, Brunello Cucinelli, Zegna and adidas. RBC is more cautious and below FY27E consensus EBIT on Kering, Moncler, Hermes and Puma.

The RBC momentum scorecard shows Outperform-rated stocks with +19% average upside to price target, most at Richemont. Earnings momentum is lacklustre across coverage, positive for WOSG, Pandora and Puma. Relative valuation is most attractive at DOCS, Burberry, EssilorLuxottica and adidas.

Website traffic: soft luxury is healthy. Gucci +18%, YSL +18%, Bottega Veneta +23%, Fendi +34%, Celine +9%, Louis Vuitton +13%. Chanel and Burberry are sequentially softer, Brunello Cucinelli is +6% and Moncler +1%. Cartier +29% leads hard luxury, and ON Running +56% and adidas +31% lead sportswear.

Swiss watch exports in Sept-26 grew 12% y/y in value and 20% in volume, with US +86% against an easy base, China -14%, and France +128%. YTD value growth is +3%. Subdial 50 resale index was flat in September.

Macro: US softer (consumer confidence, payrolls, services PMI missed, CPI ahead). China mixed (retail sales, output and exports beat, PMI missed, property soft). Europe stable to softer with inflation rising. Luxury car deliveries to China fell 22% y/y.
Input costs: WTI around $103/bbl (+66% y/y), polyester +57%, Baltic Dry +27% on Iran War disruption, cotton +20%, wool +22%, viscose +26%. Gold and silver are elevated but below recent peaks.

FX: the USD is up 3% YTD, a translation tailwind for EssilorLuxottica, Pandora, Dr Martens and WOSG and a headwind for Nike. A 10% EUR depreciation vs USD lifts luxury operating profit 5-10% but hurts adidas and Puma EBIT.

Valuation: European luxury trades at 20x 12-month forward P/E, 1 standard deviation below its average, at a 42% premium to MSCI Europe versus an 83% historical premium. Western sporting goods trades at 18x, versus a 26x 10-year average.
RBC forecasts +4% weighted luxury organic growth for FY26E and FY27E (consensus +5% for FY27E), with wide divergence led by Brunello Cucinelli, Zegna and Richemont.
Upcoming catalysts: Pandora 3Q26 on 4-Nov, Burberry 2Q/1H27E on 12-Nov, Richemont 2Q/1H27E on 13-Nov, and the Nike CMD on 16-17 November.

market_movers.rationale: adidas FY26E and FY27E guidance confirms revenue momentum and earnings growth at 13.7x CY27E P/E. Preferred sporting goods name on execution and FY27E visibility.
Brunello Cucinelli has strong revenue growth with lower volatility and a 100% HNWI customer base. Risks are US overexposure and a valuation premium.
EssilorLuxottica offers defensive attributes, with Core growth of +6.5% organic in 3Q26 and margin upside. Risks are AI smartglasses competition and gross margin dilution from Wearables.
Richemont has the strongest revenue momentum in luxury and resilient jewellery demand. Risks are gold and CHF headwinds and elevated expectations.
Zegna brand DTC organic growth is at the high end of peers, with a path to positive EBIT at Tom Ford and Thom Browne. Risk is the low end of FY27E EBIT guidance if the turnaround takes longer.
Ferrari is named among preferred luxury coverage and shows 22% implied return in the valuation table.
Burberry is a back-to-basics turnaround that may take longer in a tough luxury environment. Results are due 12-Nov.
Dr Martens has a credible new strategy but limited visibility on margins. It screens among the most attractive on relative valuation.
Hermes topline momentum is moderating and its growth premium is converging to the sector. RBC is below FY27E consensus EBIT.
Kering's turnaround timing is hard to predict. FY26E target is hard to underwrite and RBC sees downside risk to FY27E consensus.
LVMH has sequential topline acceleration against low comparatives but negative earnings revisions and downside risk to FY27E expectations.
Moncler has strong brand equity but moderating underlying growth and tough China comparatives. RBC is below FY27E consensus EBIT.
Nike's turnaround is taking longer, with a deeper China reset. Lifestyle newness is not expected until Spring/Summer 27 and the CMD on 16-17 November is the next catalyst.
Pandora has a new CEO and rebased guidance, but retail like-for-likes are flattish with negative volumes. RBC EPS is below consensus.
Puma is in reset mode with a new CEO and an Anta stake of 29%. RBC is below FY27E consensus EBIT.
Swatch has improved cost base and commercial initiatives but has likely lost share and faces Rolex supply competition at Omega.
Watches of Switzerland has a structural growth story, but the watch cycle is hard to predict and the Rolex-Bucherer deal creates a valuation overhang.

sector_views.rationale: Divergence favours absolute luxury (Brunello Cucinelli, Zegna, Richemont) over fashion-oriented luxury. China, US wealth effects and EMEA weakness are headwinds.
Prefers adidas on execution and valuation. Nike and Puma risk/reward is balanced pending an inflexion in trends. Lifestyle footwear inventories and promotions weigh on wholesale.
EssilorLuxottica is defensive with Core growth, a cleaner setup and potential margin upside, and the debate is shifting away from Wearables.

earnings_insights: adidas 3Q26 reported ahead of consensus with FY26E guidance raised. RBC FY26E EPS is 9.22 vs consensus 9.32 (estimates, EUR) and FY27E EPS 12.25 vs consensus 11.81.
Nike 1Q27 reported a miss with an FY27E outlook downgrade. RBC FY27E EPS is 1.23 vs consensus 1.25 and FY28E EPS 1.64 vs consensus 1.50 (estimates, USD).
Puma 3Q26 reported topline ahead of consensus but EBIT missed on elevated opex. RBC FY26E EBIT is -69m vs consensus -102m (estimates, EUR).
EssilorLuxottica 3Q26 reported Core organic growth of +6.5% and a Wearables contribution of +0.7%. RBC FY26E EPS is 7.12 vs consensus 7.24 (estimates, EUR).
Brunello Cucinelli and Zegna reported 3Q26 beats. Brunello Cucinelli FY26E EPS is 2.30 vs consensus 2.33 (RBC estimate, EUR). Zegna FY26E EPS is 0.42 vs consensus 0.41 (RBC estimate, USD).
Hermes, Kering, LVMH and Moncler reported mixed or in-line 3Q26 results. Consensus EPS revisions over the last month were negative for Kering (-9%), LVMH (-5%) and Hermes (-4%).
Pandora 3Q26 results are due 4-Nov. RBC FY26E EPS is DKK 58.53 vs consensus 65.30, 10% below (estimates).
Burberry 2Q/1H27E is due 12-Nov and Richemont 2Q/1H27E is due 13-Nov. RBC FY27E (March year-end) EPS for Richemont is 7.52 vs consensus 7.53 (estimates, EUR).

vol_and_positioning: Investor interest in luxury is largely hedge fund oriented, with positioning skewed to defensive names (Brunello Cucinelli, Zegna).
Sentiment and positioning in LVMH are soft relative to historic norms. Richemont carries investor crowding and elevated expectations.
RBC 30-day RSI is positive for Kering, EssilorLuxottica, LVMH and Puma depending on the exhibit, and flat or negative elsewhere.
geopolitical: Iran War and Middle East disruption weigh on Baltic Dry freight costs, Middle East air traffic (-7.5% y/y in September) and inbound tourism.
US tariff uncertainty is cited as a risk for US-exposed names such as Brunello Cucinelli and Dr Martens.
Anta's 29% stake in Puma, acquired from the Pinault family, makes it a strategic partner in China.
Anti-US rhetoric is cited as affecting inbound travel to Las Vegas.

tension_points.bull_case: Brunello Cucinelli, Zegna and Hermes Leather outperform on a 100% HNWI client base and mix gains, with Richemont jewellery resilient and RBC picking them.
tension_points.bear_case: Fashion-oriented luxury (LVMH, Kering) faces China weakness, US wealth effects and negative EPS revisions, and defensives carry premium valuations.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A China macro improvement or a sequential inflexion in LVMH and Kering trends would revive cyclical luxury.

tension_points.bull_case: FY26E and FY27E guidance confirms revenue momentum, with share opportunity in North America and gross margin tailwinds from FY27E at about 14x P/E.
tension_points.bear_case: Topline is moderating after the Terrace peak, raw material costs may cap FY27E gross margin upside, and the 10% EBIT margin target is already in estimates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Footwear failing to accelerate into FY27E to offset Apparel normalisation.

tension_points.bull_case: Zegna brand organic growth is strong and Tom Ford and Thom Browne are past peak headwinds, with a sector-leading +18% EBIT CAGR at 21.5x CY27E P/E.
tension_points.bear_case: Results rely on the Zegna brand, and Tom Ford and Thom Browne are exposed to the macro cycle and aspirational clients.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Low end of FY27E EBIT guidance at risk if the Tom Ford and Thom Browne turnaround takes longer.

tension_points.bull_case: Core growth of +6.5% organic is sustainable at mid-single digit with possible margin upside and a defensive profile.
tension_points.bear_case: Smartglasses competition is hard to disprove and Wearables mix lowers gross margins.

theme_stances.key_argument: Growth is diverging between absolute luxury and fashion-oriented luxury, and RBC prefers Brunello Cucinelli and Zegna.
theme_stances.evidence: widening growth divergence between absolute luxury

theme_stances.key_argument: adidas is executing well with sell-in discipline and offers earnings growth at a discounted valuation.
China was the main drag and will likely persist near term absent macro improvement.
